_about: Enforced triangle budgets per asset kind and LOD, and the LOD switch distances (metres at lodBias 1; the PC quality level uses lodBias 2, which doubles them). The Blender build and the Unity tests both read this file. Decision LP2.

chair._about: Up close raised from 800 to 1,600 (the owner, 2026-09-29) so the grips can be modelled: only chairs within the first switch distance use it; the far levels, which most chairs on a line use, are unchanged. Polish (2026-10-23, owner): the far level 60 -> 120 for a backrest, and a 30-triangle speck out to 800 m so the chairs no longer vanish at 300 m (as the D6 chair).

snowgun._about: Hundreds of snow guns on a mountain: a few hundred triangles up close, switching early; far out the lance is one bar. The lance is the only moving part (LOD0-2).

tower_head._about: Many towers per lift and 16 round sheaves on the heaviest heads: switching earlier than terminals keeps a whole line of 20 towers near 30k triangles in view; sheaves spin only at LOD0.

terminal_footing._about: A terminal's concrete footing, its own prefab since the piers became really tall (P3-07): below grade, so one plain level and no shadows.

terminal_detach._about: A detachable's terminal (the Sessellift D6, owner LM4): about 22 m of station under one hood, so 1.5 times a fixed-grip terminal's budget; only two per lift.

chair_detach._about: A detachable six-seat chair (the Sessellift D6): the detachable grip and a bench half as wide again as the quad's. Raised by the owner (2026-10-21, round 3): round springs, the padded bench and the grip's rollers up close, the backrest at LOD2, and a 30-triangle speck so a line reads out to 1.2 km (about 16k chair triangles a lift at High).

tower_head_wide._about: The wide-gauge heads (the Sessellift D6 at 5.6 m, owner LM3 and LM5): a crossarm with walkways and railings, and up to 12 sheaves a rope.

surface_terminal._about: A surface lift's terminal (the Monta T-bar's drive and return, the rope tow's and the carpet's ends; surface lifts, owner 2026-11-02): one bullwheel and a small frame, about half a chairlift terminal. LOD0 holds to 20 m, as a chairlift terminal's (Gate 3, 2026-11-03): the T-bar's stations are 18-20 m across, too big to hand over at 15 m.

surface_tower_head._about: A T-bar tower head (owner 2026-11-02; raised for the two-level head, D10 2026-11-03, and for the chair tower's lifting frame in miniature, 2026-11-03): crossarm, lifting frame, a sheave train on each rope with its catchers, the catwalk, cables; a line can have 20 or more.

surface_mast._about: One 1 m section of a T-bar tower's tube mast with its ladder; stacked to the tower's height.

surface_base._about: A T-bar tower's base: footing, pier, the leaned base plate and the mast's first 2.2 m in the red tower pad (D5).

surface_hut._about: A surface lift's operator hut (the Monta T-bar's, D9/Q3 2026-11-03): one beside a bottom station.

surface_carrier._about: A surface lift's carrier (the T-bar's recoil box on its grip, the T bar and the J bar): up to a hundred on a line, so small and early.

carpet_station._about: A magic carpet's station (the Glidepath's drive at the top and tension at the bottom, single or double, owner C1-C11 2026-11-04): a low box about 4 m long with its motor cover and cabinet, ending at its plate (the snow approach is the game's); LOD0 to 15 m.

carpet_segment._about: A magic carpet's belt module (2 m or the 1 m filler) or its side rails: about fifty on a 100 m carpet, so small and early (the double's caps; the single's need about two thirds).

carpet_gallery._about: A magic carpet's gallery bay (2 m, glass on both faces up close), its exit bay or its portal: one bay per belt module. LOD3 keeps the arch's outer face (Gate 2: the arches vanishing at 150 m showed as a band along the line).
